description: BS AI student at UST Bannu working toward ML research and a US MS/PhD. We’ll build an explainable ML tool that detects and forecasts trends in NASA Earth observation data, with clear visuals and documented, reproducible code. I handle Python, ML and explainable AI. Looking for: Earth/climate science knowledge, statistics or time-series, data visualization and front-end, and someone to polish the pitch. Serious beginners welcome. Aiming for a finished, well-documented project.
summary: Explainable Earth is an open-source web app that detects, forecasts and explains trends in NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 temperature data, built for the challenge "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!". It measures the warming trend with an autocorrelation-adjusted 95% confidence interval and forecasts ahead with a prediction band. A rolling-origin backtest chooses the forecast window and reports skill against a naive baseline, so users see how far to trust it. Its key feature is explainability: the global trend is split exactly into area-weighted latitude-band contributions. Since 1980 the world warmed about 0.19 C per decade, while the Arctic (64N-90N) warmed about 3.5 times faster from only 5% of Earth's surface. The tool helps students, journalists and analysts understand where warming comes from, not just that it happens. It is tested, deployed live, and fully reproducible.
details:
What it does: Loads NASA GISTEMP v4 zonal annual temperature anomalies (1951-1980 baseline). Tab 1 shows the trend with a 95% CI, a forecast with a prediction band, a backtest table, and a rolling 30-year trend showing acceleration. Tab 2 explains the trend: warming rate per latitude band, each band's area share versus its share of global warming, and a latitude-year heatmap. Tab 3 documents the method, limits and SI use.

How it works: OLS trend with a confidence interval adjusted for autocorrelation; linear forecast with a prediction interval; rolling-origin backtest comparing 30-year, 50-year and all-year windows against a naive baseline. Global slope = sum(area share x band slope), an exact decomposition validated against NASA's own global series.

Impact: Makes climate trends transparent and checkable for education, journalism and analysis.

Tools: Python 3.12, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Plotly, Streamlit, pytest, Hypothesis, ruff, mypy, Docker, GitHub, Streamlit Community Cloud.

Creativity: An auditable, exact explanation layer instead of a black box, plus an honest backtest.

Limits: Linear extrapolation, surface temperature only, descriptive not causal.

Code: https://github.com/MuhammadYasirKhan-ai/explainable-earth

Live app: https://explainable-earth.streamlit.app/
